# Shopping data: feeds, markup and Storebot

Product rich results and Google Images product annotations come from product structured data without Merchant Center, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed (said at the event; Google's docs recommend feed and markup together for the widest eligibility). Because AI Mode answers detailed follow-up questions, Google added a few flexible Merchant Center attributes in 2026 instead of hundreds of narrow ones: question and answer, document link, related product, item group title, variant option and popularity rank; it now also stresses product highlights and key-value product details, and its help marks most of these as intended for conversational experiences such as AI Mode. Data quality matters more for AI and agents ('garbage in, garbage out'). Google Shopping crawls with Storebot-Google, which recrawls more often for prices and availability, validates feeds and crawls cart and checkout pages. Google said most new attributes can also be used from schema.org markup, but its Merchant Center help lists a schema.org property only for item_group_title. Google announced the conversational attributes in January 2026 and opened them to retailers globally at Google Marketing Live on 20 May 2026; in testing with lululemon, brand-submitted attributes were used in 50% of relevant AI Mode product recommendations (Google's September 2026 post). Google's help sets the limits: up to 30 question-and-answer pairs per product, up to five PDF document links, and a popularity rank that is the merchant's own 0-100 ranking against its inventory, not a sales figure across shops. This builds on Day 2's merchant markup news, such as sale-price validity dates aligned with Merchant Center.

Based on: `D3-C343`, `D3-C346`, `D3-C344`, `D3-C357`, `D3-C363`, `D3-C365`, `D3-C367`, `D3-C392`, `D3-C394`, `D3-C358`, `D3-C385`, `D3-C386`, `D3-C387`, `D3-C388`, `D3-C380`, `D3-C381`, `D3-C361`, `D3-C362`, `D3-C408`, `D3-C369`, `D3-C371`, `D3-C375`, `D3-C376`, `D2-C506`.

## What to do

- Keep price, availability, brand and GTIN identical in the feed and in on-page markup, then add Q&As, highlights, product details and related products.
- Do not block Storebot-Google on product, cart or checkout paths.
- Fill the Q&A attribute from real customer questions, answered factually per product.

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** Google's free listings help says crawled store products can appear on Google without markup or Merchant Center but does not say whether that includes the Shopping tab; for a shop that wants Shopping tab visibility, the stage rule that Merchant Center is required is the safe working assumption.
  <br><sub>`D3-C348` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en), [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For an online shop, Product structured data is enough for product rich results and Google Images product annotations, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed too; keep feed and markup values identical, since Google can use the markup to validate the feed.
  <br><sub>`D3-C351` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's January 2026 announcement spoke of 'dozens' of new Merchant Center attributes, while the Day 3 talk counted six; all six named on stage (question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, item_group_title, variant_option, popularity_rank) are in the Merchant Center product data specification as of 3 October 2026.
  <br><sub>`D3-C366` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links · [New tech and tools for retailers to succeed in an agentic shopping era](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/agentic-commerce-ai-tools-protocol-retailers-platforms/), [Product data specification](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7052112?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** On stage the popularity rank was framed as how well a product sells on a marketplace, but Google's documentation defines it as the merchant's own 0-100 ranking against the rest of its inventory: a self-reported, relative value, not a sales figure across shops.
  <br><sub>`D3-C376` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links · [Popularity rank [popularity_rank]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085297?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** As of 3 October 2026 Google's Merchant Center help lists no schema.org property for question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, popularity_rank, variant_option or product_detail (only item_group_title maps, to ProductGroup.name), and Search Central does not document such markup: reading these attributes from schema.org is a stage statement, the feed is the documented route.
  <br><sub>`D3-C381` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links · [Question and answer [question_and_answer]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085211?hl=en), [Document link [document_link]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17084656?hl=en), [Related product [related_product]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085213?hl=en), [Popularity rank [popularity_rank]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085297?hl=en), [Variant option [variant_option]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085214?hl=en), [Product detail [product_detail]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9218260?hl=en), [Item group title [item_group_title]](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/17085146?hl=en), [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SHP-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Treat Storebot-Google separately from Googlebot in robots.txt and bot protection: a shop that blocks it on product, cart or checkout paths can undermine Shopping price and availability checks, even when Googlebot is allowed.
  <br><sub>`D3-C390` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links · Used by `DEV-SHP-02`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Shop developers should first keep core feed and markup values (price, availability, brand, GTIN) accurate, then add Q&As, product highlights, specs as key-value product details and related products in the Merchant Center feed, and mirror them in schema.org Product markup only as Google documents support for it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C410` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Content teams can feed the new Q&A attribute from real customer questions (support tickets, reviews, sales chats), answered factually per product; this is the detailed, merchant-owned data Google said AI shopping answers need.
  <br><sub>`D3-C411` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-SHP-01`: Use Product markup for rich results and a Merchant Center feed for the Shopping tab, with identical values
- Requirement `DEV-SHP-02`: Let Storebot-Google crawl product, cart and checkout pages, through robots.txt and bot protection
- Requirement `DEV-SHP-03`: Send conversational product data in the Merchant Center feed: Q&A, product details, highlights and related products
- Requirement `DEV-SHP-04`: Treat product Q&A and specification markup in schema.org as an extra on top of the feed
- Glossary term *Conversational attributes*
- Glossary term *Merchant Center*
- Glossary term *Product highlights and product details*
- Glossary term *Storebot-Google*
- Glossary term *Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)*
